title: [Bug] use_fused_kernels=True causes training quality regression when ulysses_sequence_parallel_size > 1 for Qwen3-VL GRPO
body: ### System Info ----------Python Info---------- Version : 3.12.3 Compiler : GCC 13.3.0 Build : ('main', 'Nov 3 2025 11:03:51') Arch : ('64bit', 'ELF') ------------Pip Info----------- Version : 24.0 Directory : /usr/local/lib/python3.12/site-packages/pip vllm : 0.11.0+cu129 sglang : not found. ray : 2.49.2 torch : 2.8.0 ----------verl Info----------- Version : 0.8.0.dev Directory : /[redacted]/verl/verl Commit Hash : 4b9c14f2c306d43f84eccf47315323e3f1ce1270 ----------Platform Info---------- Platform : Linux-5.10.134-013.7.2.[redacted].x86_64-x86_64-with-glibc2.39 system : Linux node : [redacted] release : 5.10.134-013.7.2.[redacted].x86_64 version : #1 SMP Sat Feb 28 03:27:43 UTC 2026 ----------Environment---------- CUDA Runtime : 12.9 CUDA Compiler : Cuda compilation tools, release 12.9, V12.9.0 ### Information - [ ] The official example scripts - [x] My own modified scripts ### Tasks - [ ] An officially supported task in the `examples` folder (such as GLUE/SQuAD, ...) - [x] My own task or dataset (give details below) ### Reproduction We observed this issue while training a vision-language GRPO task in `verl`. - Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct` - Dataset: an internal anonymized multimodal multiple-choice dataset (similar in task format to `Geo3K`) - Input: text + image - Output: text - Reward: based on whether the final multiple-choice answer is correct, using `\boxed{}` extraction / detection This issue does not manifest as a crash or exception. The training job runs successfully, but the problem is a **consistent training quality regression**: when `ulysses_sequence_parallel_size > 1` is combined with `use_fused_kernels=True`, both reward and validation score keep decreasing. About the attached figure: - The rising curves are all `SP=1` - The descending curves are all `SP>1 + use_fused_kernels=True`, where `SP>1` includes `SP=2`, `4`, and `8` We also performed step-by-step ablations over many related parameters, including different `batch_size` settings and multiple relevant feature toggles. After these controlled comparisons, the issue consistently pointed to `use_fused_kernels`. Steps to reproduce: 1. Use the same training setup with: ```bash train_sp=1 actor_rollout_ref.model.use_fused_kernels=True actor_rollout_ref.actor.ulysses_sequence_parallel_size=${train_sp} actor_rollout_ref.ref.ulysses_sequence_parallel_size=${train_sp} ``` Result on our side: training behaves normally, reward increases, and validation score improves. 2. Keep the rest of the training setup unchanged, but change it to: ```bash train_sp=2 # also reproduced with 4 and 8 actor_rollout_ref.model.use_fused_kernels=True actor_rollout_ref.actor.ulysses_sequence_parallel_size=${train_sp} actor_rollout_ref.ref.ulysses_sequence_parallel_size=${train_sp} ``` Result on our side: training still runs successfully, but reward and validation score consistently decrease. 3. Keep the rest of the training setup unchanged, keep `SP>1`, but disable fused kernels: ```bash train_sp=2 # also verified with 4 and 8 actor_rollout_ref.model.use_fused_kernels=False actor_rollout_ref.actor.ulysses_sequence_parallel_size=${train_sp} actor_rollout_ref.ref.ulysses_sequence_parallel_size=${train_sp} ``` Result on our side: the regression disappears and training behavior returns to normal. The full training script is as follows: ```bash #!/usr/bin/env bash set -xeu # Install local verl source pip install --no-deps -e /path/to/local/verl # Training and validation data train_path="[/path/to/internal_multimodal_train.parquet]" test_path="[/path/to/internal_multimodal_val.parquet]" # Base model MODEL_BASE="Qwen/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct" # Project / experiment name PROJECT_NAME="ANON_MM_TASK" EXPR_NAME="$(basename "${MODEL_BASE}")-GRPO_bsz128_TP1SP1_4NODES_0420" # Output directories RUN_DIR=/path/to/output_root DEFAULT_LOCAL_DIR="${RUN_DIR}/checkpoints/${PROJECT_NAME}/${EXPR_NAME}" ROLLOUT_DATA_DIR="${RUN_DIR}/log/${PROJECT_NAME}/${EXPR_NAME}/rollout" VALIDATION_DATA_DIR="${RUN_DIR}/log/${PROJECT_NAME}/${EXPR_NAME}/validation" export TENSORBOARD_DIR="${RUN_DIR}/tensorboard_log/${PROJECT_NAME}/${EXPR_NAME}" # Generation parameters max_prompt_length=16384 max_response_length=4096 temperature=1.0 top_p=1.0 top_k=-1 # 0 for HF rollout, -1 for vLLM rollout val_top_p=0.7 # Algorithm parameters train_batch_size=128 train_mini_batch_size=32 clip_ratio_low=0.2 clip_ratio_high=0.28 clip_ratio_c=3.0 entropy_coeff=0 grad_clip=1.0 loss_agg_mode=token-mean use_kl_in_reward=False kl_coef=0.001 use_kl_loss=False kl_loss_coef=0.001 # Engineering parameters, mainly related to speed / memory / OOM rollout_tp=1 train_sp=1 use_dynamic_bsz=True max_token_len=$((max_prompt_length + max_response_length)) actor_ppo_max_token_len=$(( max_token_len / train_sp )) infer_ppo_max_token_len=$(( max_token_len / train_sp )) rollout_max_num_batched_tokens=${max_token_len} offload=True python3 -m verl.trainer.main_ppo \ algorithm.adv_estimator=grpo \ algorithm.use_kl_in_reward=${use_kl_in_reward} \ algorithm.kl_ctrl.kl_coef=${kl_coef} \ data.train_files=${train_path} \ data.val_files=${test_path} \ data.train_batch_size=${train_batch_size} \ data.max_prompt_length=${max_prompt_length} \ data.max_response_length=${max_response_length} \ data.filter_overlong_prompts=True \ data.truncation='error' \ data.image_key=images \ actor_rollout_ref.model.path=${MODEL_BASE} \ actor_rollout_ref.actor.optim.lr=1e-6 \ actor_rollout_ref.model.use_remove_padding=True \ actor_rollout_ref.model.use_fused_kernels=False \ actor_rollout_ref.model.enable_gradient_checkpointing=True \ actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_mini_batch_size=${train_mini_batch_size} \ actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_micro_batch_size_per_gpu=1 \ actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_dynamic_bsz=${use_dynamic_bsz} \ actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_max_token_len_per_gpu=${actor_ppo_max_token_len} \ actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_kl_loss=${use_kl_loss} \ actor_rollout_ref.actor.kl_loss_coef=${kl_loss_coef} \ actor_rollout_ref.actor.clip_ratio_low=${clip_ratio_low} \ actor_rollout_ref.actor.clip_ratio_high=${clip_ratio_high} \ actor_rollout_ref.actor.clip_ratio_c=${clip_ratio_c} \ actor_rollout_ref.actor.entropy_coeff=${entropy_coeff} \ actor_rollout_ref.actor.grad_clip=${grad_clip} \ actor_rollout_ref.actor.loss_agg_mode=${loss_agg_mode} \ actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.param_offload=${offload} \ actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.optimizer_offload=${offload} \ actor_rollout_ref.rollout.tensor_model_parallel_size=${rollout_tp} \ actor_rollout_ref.actor.ulysses_sequence_parallel_size=${train_sp} \ actor_rollout_ref.ref.ulysses_sequence_parallel_size=${train_sp} \ actor_rollout_ref.rollout.name=vllm \ +actor_rollout_ref.rollout.engine_kwargs.vllm.disable_mm_preprocessor_cache=True \ actor_rollout_ref.rollout.gpu_memory_utilization=0.8 \ actor_rollout_ref.rollout.enable_chunked_prefill=True \ actor_rollout_ref.rollout.enforce_eager=False \ actor_rollout_ref.rollout.free_cache_engine=True \ actor_rollout_ref.rollout.log_prob_micro_batch_size_per_gpu=1 \ actor_rollout_ref.rollout.log_prob_use_dynamic_bsz=${use_dynamic_bsz} \ actor_rollout_ref.rollout.log_prob_max_token_len_per_gpu=${infer_ppo_max_token_len} \ actor_rollout_ref.rollout.max_num_batched_tokens=${rollout_max_num_batched_tokens} \ actor_rollout_ref.rollout.temperature=${temperature} \ actor_rollout_ref.rollout.top_p=${top_p} \ actor_rollout_ref.rollout.top_k=${top_k} \ actor_rollout_ref.rollout.val_kwargs.temperature=${temperature} \ actor_rollout_ref.rollout.val_kwargs.top_p=${val_top_p} \ actor_rollout_ref.rollout.val_kwargs.top_k=${top_k} \ actor_rollout_ref.rollout.val_kwargs.do_sample=True \ actor_rollout_ref.rollout.val_kwargs.n=1 \ actor_rollout_ref.rollout.n=8 \ actor_rollout_ref.ref.log_prob_micro_batch_size_per_gpu=1 \ actor_rollout_ref.ref.log_prob_use_dynamic_bsz=${use_dynamic_bsz} \ actor_rollout_ref.ref.log_prob_max_token_len_per_gpu=${infer_ppo_max_token_len} \ actor_rollout_ref.ref.fsdp_config.param_offload=${offload} \ trainer.critic_warmup=0 \ trainer.logger='["console","tensorboard"]' \ trainer.project_name=${PROJECT_NAME} \ trainer.experiment_name=${EXPR_NAME} \ trainer.default_local_dir=${DEFAULT_LOCAL_DIR} \ trainer.rollout_data_dir=${ROLLOUT_DATA_DIR} \ trainer.validation_data_dir=${VALIDATION_DATA_DIR} \ +ray_kwargs.ray_init.runtime_env.env_vars.TENSORBOARD_DIR=${TENSORBOARD_DIR} \ trainer.n_gpus_per_node=16 \ trainer.nnodes=4 \ trainer.save_freq=20 \ trainer.test_freq=5 \ trainer.total_epochs=100 $@ ``` There is no error message or stack trace, because this is not a runtime failure but a correctness / quality issue during training. ### Expected behavior `ulysses_sequence_parallel_size` should mainly be a parallelism / engineering knob, and under the same overall training setup it should not systematically damage training quality. More specifically, changing from `SP=1` to `SP=2`, `4`, or `8` should not cause reward and validation score to consistently degrade only when `use_fused_kernels=True`; at minimum, the same setup should not exhibit such a stable quality regression. If the combination of `use_fused_kernels` and `SP>1` is currently unsupported for some VLM paths, it would be helpful to either: - raise a clear error or warning - document the limitation explicitly - or automatically fall back to a safe implementation on the affected path
